title: Broad service bindings and host-port defaults
impact: Development database/admin/documentation services may be reachable from other machines when run on an exposed host. Actual Internet exposure was not tested.
fix: Default host publishing/listening to 127.0.0.1; expose host ports via environment; validate Strapi listener port range; retain standard database container ports as protocol constants.
remaining_risk: Explicit HOST=0.0.0.0 or DATABASE_BIND_ADDRESS overrides remain possible for controlled containers. IPv6, firewall and container routing need review.

title: Known credentials and weak example signing keys
impact: If examples/defaults are deployed unchanged, attackers may guess SQL credentials or signing keys. These are known example values, not confirmed live secrets.
fix: Require unique SQL/Compose passwords; remove secret fallbacks; require 32-character admin secrets and two strong app keys in affected example configs. Require operator-selected database image references.
remediation_state: Source-remediated in listed configs; rotation required
remaining_risk: Previously used keys/passwords must be rotated and sessions invalidated. Placeholder .env examples and v4 migration fixture inputs still need operator review. Length does not prove entropy.

title: Credentialed CORS reflects arbitrary origins
code:
origin: '*', credentials: true
if (normalizedOrigins.includes('*')) return requestOrigin;
impact: A hostile website can receive credentialed responses if relevant credentials are available cross-site. Exploitability depends on cookie settings and affected routes.
fix: Deny cross-origin requests by default; disable credentials by default; reject null/absent origins; require explicit origin allowlist for credentialed requests, including dynamic configuration.
remaining_risk: Cross-origin frontends need an explicit trusted list. CORS is not authentication or CSRF protection. Alternate GraphQL/custom middleware paths require retest.

title: URL-import SSRF redirect and DNS-validation gaps
code:
await dns.lookup(parsedUrl.hostname);
await doFetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS) });
impact: A public URL can redirect to private/link-local services. Validation and fetch resolve separately, creating a DNS-rebinding window. Import endpoint authorization affects reachability.
fix: Reject redirects; check every returned DNS address; add unspecified, CGNAT, multicast and reserved blocks. Focused tests cover blocked answers and redirect option forwarding.
remaining_risk: Fetch still resolves independently and proxies may resolve differently. Use a connection-time validated/pinned resolver plus destination allowlist and egress firewall, or disable URL imports until then. Outgoing webhooks need separate destination policy.

title: Reset tokens lack expiry and atomic consumption
code:
findOne({ where: { resetPasswordToken: code } });
await getService('user').edit(user.id, { resetPasswordToken: null, password });
impact: A leaked unused reset link had no time limit. Parallel reads can both succeed before token clearing, violating one-time use.
fix: Add private resetPasswordTokenExpiresAt datetime field; issue links with 15-minute default (1-3600 seconds configurable); reject missing/invalid/expired expiry; clear token and expiry after change.
remaining_risk: Old links are deliberately invalidated. Atomic token consumption, confirmation-token expiry, timing uniformity and legacy JWT invalidation remain open. Apply database schema migration safely before enabling this patch.

title: Export encryption uses unauthenticated legacy modes
impact: ECB reveals repeating plaintext patterns and provides no integrity. Optional CBC variants use key-derived IVs. Export confidentiality/integrity depends on safe storage and strong passphrases.
fix: Not changed in this overlay: design a versioned archive format using authenticated encryption, random KDF salt/nonce, calibrated KDF, and coordinated importer/exporter migration with compatibility tests.
remaining_risk: Do not treat existing encrypted exports as authenticated. Protect storage/access and migrate trusted legacy archives; changing one default would break import compatibility. Admin AES-GCM service is separate and was not confused with export encryption.

title: GraphQL depth and pagination unbounded by default
impact: Enabled GraphQL installations can accept expensive shapes/pagination; baseline bootstrap warns rather than requiring finite limits. No load testing occurred.
fix: Set defaultLimit:25, maxLimit:100 and depthLimit:10; disable production introspection and HTTP batching; explicitly enable Apollo CSRF prevention.
remaining_risk: Depth is not cost. Alias/fragment amplification, query timeouts, per-operation throttling and schema suggestions remain to address. Explicit app overrides can defeat defaults.

title: Logout reports success when revocation throws
code:
catch (err) { strapi.log.error('UP logout failed', err); }
return ctx.send({ ok: true });
impact: Users could believe they logged out even though a backend revocation error left sessions usable. Only the refresh-mode path is relevant to this error handler.
fix: Throw a generic application error after logging revocation exceptions, preventing a false success response.
remaining_risk: Non-throwing unsuccessful revocation returns and actual token invalidation must be checked. Stateless legacy mode still cannot offer server-side logout/revocation guarantees.

title: Long-lived legacy tokens and script-readable storage
impact: Long-lived bearer tokens increase theft/replay impact; localStorage tokens are readable by any successful same-origin script compromise. No XSS exploit is established.
fix: Open: migrate clients to short-lived access tokens with refresh rotation/reuse detection; use server-set HttpOnly Secure cookies with CSRF protection where appropriate; require issuer/audience and test revocation.
remaining_risk: Do not globally flip token mode without updating clients. Legacy JWTs may survive password changes; environment-specific claim and key rotation policy is needed.

title: Dependency advisory matches need reachability triage
code:
2,838 resolved npm package/version pairs queried
44 matching pairs; 111 unique advisory IDs
impact: Known advisory records affect locked versions, including runtime and build/test dependencies. A lock match is not proof the vulnerable function is exposed in the app.
fix: Open: identify direct/transitive dependency chains, inspect affected functions/ranges, upgrade to upstream-reviewed fixed versions, regenerate locks using Yarn, and run full regression tests.
remediation_state: Open — advisory matches, not confirmed exploits
remaining_risk: No automated version bumps were made. Nested example/docs lockfiles and actual deployment dependency graph remain unscanned. Do not infer all advisories have High severity from this aggregate priority.

title: Documentation CSP permits inline/CDN scripts
impact: The documentation/playground CSP is weaker than the checklist baseline, reducing defense against injection or compromised third-party scripts. No script-execution exploit was demonstrated.
fix: Open: remove unnecessary documentation/playground routes in production, then migrate required UI scripts to nonce/hash policy and reviewed exact CDN origins/SRI.
remaining_risk: Blindly removing inline permissions can break Swagger/Apollo interfaces. Render and test each actual production surface after policy changes.

title: Local upload provider serves from application public directory
impact: If active content is accepted and served inline from the app origin, uploads can expand browser trust risk. Content type, CSP and payload behavior must be tested; no stored XSS is asserted.
fix: Open: select separate non-executable upload origin/bucket, deny or sanitize active SVG/HTML, enforce nosniff/Content-Disposition and per-download authorization as needed.
remaining_risk: Changing provider URLs/storage requires migration and client validation. MIME detection alone is not active-content sanitization.
